Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.

This review describes how single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, especially scATAC-seq, has been used to map the regulatory programs controlling bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration, and how these programs go awry in skeletal diseases. It synthesizes the emerging single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas of bone, highlighting transcription factor binding and gene regulatory landscapes that determine bone cell fate and function.

A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.

This paper develops a knowledge graph focused on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) for hypertension with emotional comorbidities such as anxiety, depression, and insomnia, organizing syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs along with their literature sources. It then evaluates the knowledge graph's contribution to generated answers through a blinded question-answering assessment. The work demonstrates a domain-specific approach to structuring TCM knowledge and assessing its utility in downstream QA systems.

Plant biotechnology journal 2026-Oct-28 Medium

Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.

This paper describes how the CABBI research center organized a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework to engineer C4 grasses (such as sugarcane, sorghum, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol (oil) in vegetative tissues for renewable fuels and bioproducts. It highlights the need to coordinate molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program, and distills lessons learned from applying this integrated approach across multiple feedstocks.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-Oct-27 Medium

Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.

The authors compute phenologs—statistical overlaps between human disease genes and model-organism phenotype genes linked by orthology—at scale using the Monarch Knowledge Graph, which integrates gene-disease, gene-phenotype, and orthology data across human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as an orthology framework, they produce a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases. This provides a broad, principled resource for cross-species disease gene discovery.

OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.

OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that consolidates literature-derived evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable records. Each finding is linked to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities along with supporting text, enabling auditable and reusable evidence for zoonotic emergence research.

Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.

This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict the onset of acute kidney injury and to forecast patient prognosis after AKI occurs. The approach addresses the high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity of EHR data that challenge conventional machine learning methods.

Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.

This paper develops a Meta Mesh Ontology designed to integrate mental health knowledge across different domains, addressing the limitations of rigid categorical systems like DSM-5 and ICD-11. The ontology aims to capture the multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and comorbidity patterns of psychiatric disorders. It is evaluated as a framework for cross-domain knowledge integration in mental health.

scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.

scSpatial is a new atlas/database that consolidates single-cell spatial omics datasets, which were previously scattered across individual publications. It integrates spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities to support construction of spatially resolved cell atlases and characterization of disease-associated tissue remodeling. The resource aims to make SCSO data more accessible and reusable for the community.

AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance.

This preprint presents an evidence-aware AI framework that integrates heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data—FAERS adverse event reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and electronic health records—using LLM-based information extraction and ontology-driven semantic harmonization. The work aims to produce a reliable knowledge resource for drug safety signal detection despite differences in data structure, terminology, and evidence quality across sources.

The Drosophila Secretome.

This preprint presents a systematic computational assembly of the Drosophila secretome by integrating FlyBase, UniProt, and Gene Ontology annotations with large-scale proteomics datasets. The resulting resource catalogs secreted proteins in the fly, many of which are conserved in humans, providing a foundation for studying development, immunity, and disease in a model organism.

Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.

This review argues that precision nutrition—tailoring dietary advice using multi-omics, wearables, and AI/ML—has advanced rapidly in discovery but lags in clinical translation because evidence is fragmented across life stages and poorly integrated with systems biology. The authors call for lifespan-spanning frameworks that account for how nutritional needs and response heterogeneity change from preconception onward.

Ontology- and Data-Driven Circularity Assessment of Waste-Derived Rigid PVC-u: A Micro-Macro Decision Framework for Sustainable Recycling and Smart Manufacturing.

This paper presents a framework for assessing the circularity of recycled rigid PVC-u, combining a Protégé-based ontology with big data analytics to organize knowledge about materials, recycling processes, quality, and sustainability criteria. It aims to support decision-making across technical, environmental, and economic dimensions for sustainable recycling and smart manufacturing. The work is a domain-specific decision-support framework rather than a broadly generalizable methodological advance.

WingShape-Warn: A Morphology-Driven Early-Warning Pipeline for Mosquito-Borne Disease Surveillance.

WingShape-Warn is an open-source, reproducible pipeline that combines geometric morphometrics with deep learning-based image analysis to quantify mosquito wing shape from images. The authors propose that wing morphology shifts driven by environmental stressors can act as early-warning indicators of mosquito abundance and arboviral outbreak risk, aiming to bring quantitative wing-shape analysis into operational surveillance. The work is a technology/code contribution rather than a field study, so its practical impact will depend on adoption and validation.

Comparative Genomic Analysis Reveals Evolutionary Features of Glugea plecoglossi, a Fish-Infecting Microsporidian Parasite of Ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis).

This study reports a new genome assembly for Glugea plecoglossi, a microsporidian parasite that infects ayu fish and forms xenomas, and compares it with 42 other microsporidian genomes. The 16.71 Mb assembly reveals evolutionary features and phylogenetic placement of this poorly characterized lineage, providing a resource for understanding genome reduction and variation among microsporidia.

Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.

ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized agents over a network-driven workflow. InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.

InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations covering hundreds of millions of sequences, with near-complete coverage of UniProtKB, and includes mappings to major resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for functional annotation of protein sequences across biology.

Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.

This study exposed human macrophage-like THP-1 cells to crystalline silica particles and profiled changes in microRNA expression both inside cells and in the extracellular medium. The authors identify silica-responsive miRNA signatures that could serve as biomarkers of occupational silica exposure. The work is a descriptive in vitro profiling study linking particle exposure to miRNA dysregulation.

The Journal of investigative dermatology 2026-Nov-01 Medium

Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.

This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes trigger rapid extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps induced by the two strains displayed distinct proteomic programs, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in acne pathogenesis.

Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.

This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reframed not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. Under this view, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs, potentially reshaping how mechanistic drug-development models are parameterized.

PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.

PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps residues between UniProt protein sequences and Protein Data Bank structures. It uses faster sequence search (MMseqs2), an improved scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and refinement based on backbone connectivity to produce more accurate residue-level mappings. This makes the historically internal PDBe pipeline available to the broader community.

EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.

EchoGO is a reproducible framework for functional enrichment of transcriptomic data that runs GOseq enrichment while comparing results across multiple user-selected organism annotation contexts, using experiment-specific backgrounds. It assembles evidence at the GO-term level together with analytical and organism provenance, helping address incomplete annotation, inconsistent identifier recognition, and uncertainty about which annotation resource is most informative.

Integrating cure and care in Alzheimer's disease: a systems perspective for precision medicine.

This perspective article argues that Alzheimer's disease research should move beyond amyloid and tau to a systems framework incorporating neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions. The authors propose integrating AI, multi-omics, and digital biomarkers to support precision medicine that combines disease-modifying treatment with care, while cautioning that simply aggregating data modalities does not capture the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease.
